 ​2​                             ​PERSONAL INFORMATION:​

 ​3​​Q. Please state your name and address.​

 ​4​​A​.​​My name is Hank Jones and Elizabeth Jones. My address is 2201 CR 311, Jarrell,​

 ​5​​TX (Mailing: PO Box 584, Jarrell, TX 76537​


 ​6​​Q. Have you filed a Motion to Intervene in this proceeding?​

 ​7​​A​.​​Yes.​


 ​8​​Q. What link and tracts are you testifying in representation of today?​


 ​9​​A. F8 and F45 Tract 5275 and 5276​


10​​Q. Are you testifying on behalf of anyone, or just yourself?​
​


11​​A. Our selves​
​


12​​Q. How is the property affected by the Bell County East to Big Hill 765kV​
​

13​​transmission line project proposed by Oncor and LCRA TSC?​
​


14​​A. Proposed link routes F8 and F45 traverse our property where we reside, have​
​

15​​livestock, crops, native wildlife habitation, impact the landscape and reduce property​
​

16​​value.​
​


17​​Q. What is the purpose of your testimony?​
​


18​​A. The purpose of our testimony is to explain how this proposed transmission project​
​

19​​would affect our property, livestock, crops, native wildlife habitat, community and to​
​


                                                ​Direct Testimony of Hank and Elizabeth Jones, Pro Se​
                                                                              ​PUC Docket No. 59475​
                                                                      ​SOAH Docket No.​​473-26-16349​
                                                                                         ​Page​​4​​of​​11​
  ​1​​present concerns regarding the lack of demonstrated necessity for the project, the​

 ​2​​impacts on rural landowners and agricultural operations, environmental impacts​

 ​3​​associated with constructing a large 765 kv transmission corridor through this region.​


 ​4​​Q. Did you receive notice from Oncor?​


 ​5​​A. No​


 ​6​​Q. When did you become aware of the project's impact on your land?​


 ​7​​May 19, 2026​


 ​8​​Q. How did you become aware of the project?​


 ​9​​A A prior neighbor who moved to another residence in a neighboring county that is also​

10​​potentially impacted by the route notified me.​
​


11​​Q. What have you done since you were notified?​
​


12​​A. Being overwhelmed and uninformed we filed a plea for assistance to the Texas​
​

13​​Public Utility Commission under docket 59475 and a Motion for remedy and relief due to​
​

14​​lack of notification to the State Office of Administrative Hearings.​
​


15​​Q. To date have you received notice or a landowner packet from Oncor/LCRA or​
​

16​​its coordinators?​
​


17​​A. No​
​


18​​Q. What routes do you oppose?​
​


19​​A. F8 and F45​
​

 ​1​​Q. What routes do you support?​


​2​​A. We do not support other routes but rather support the halting of the project for​

​3​​further review.​


​4​​Q. Have you ever testified at the Public Utility Commission of Texas before?​


​5​​A. No​


​6​​Q. Was this material prepared by you or under your supervision?​


​7​​A. Yes​


​8​                     ​PROPERTY DESCRIPTION AND HISTORY​

​9​​Q. Can you please describe the affected property, including the legal description​

10​​from the County CAD?​
​


11​
​     ​A.​ ​The affected property contains two parcels listed in Williamson County CAD as​

12​​AW0384 LEWIS, A.A. SUR., ACRES 14.06 (R384570) and AW0384 LEWIS, A.A.​
​

13​​SUR.,ACRES 9.86 (R403881)​
​


14​​Q. Can you please explain your history and familiarity with the affected property,​
​

15​​including its current usage?​
​


16​​A. The property has an existing original homestead dating back to 1920. We have been​
​

17​​owners and residents of the property for the past 25 years. The property has multiple​
​

18​​barns, cattle pens, gates, fences, implement sheds, natural wet weather creek, 2 cistern​
​

19​​wells and a stocktank. Cattle and crops have been ongoing for 25 years. Native wildlife​
​

  ​1​​such as fish, quail, deer, ducks, fox, armadillo, snakes, squirrel, coyote, hawks and​

 ​2​​other birds and wildlife reside on the property.​


 ​3​​Q. Can you please include any pictures with dates that depict the property and​

 ​4​​how it is used?​


 ​5​​A. Yes​


 ​6​​Q. Have the pictures been altered?​


 ​7​​A. No​


 ​8​​Q. Do the pictures accurately represent the views of the property?​


 ​9​​A. Yes​


10​
​               ​IMPACT ON LAND USE AND ECONOMICS (PURA § 37.056)​

11​​Q. How would the proposed transmission line interfere with your current land​
​

12​​use?​
​


13​​A​.​​Grazing, hay production and recreational use such as hunting, would be impacted as​
​

14​​wildlife in the area would be disturbed.​
​


15​​Q. Are there any specific structures or features that would be within 500 feet of​
​

16​​any of the proposed routes?​
​


17​​A. Our residence in which we reside, our barns and implement buildings, natural​
​

18​​waterways and stocktank.​
​


19​​Q. In your opinion, how will this project affect the value of your land?​
​

                                                  ​Direct Testimony of Hank and Elizabeth Jones, Pro Se​
                                                                                ​PUC Docket No. 59475​
                                                                        ​SOAH Docket No.​​473-26-16349​
                                                                                           ​Page​​7​​of​​11​
  ​1​​A. We believe this project, its impact on environment, disruption of soil, trees and​

 ​2​​meaningful land usage, as well as visual impacts will reduce purchasing desirability and​

 ​3​​thereby reduce not only the property value of the easement but the value of both​

 ​4​​property tracts for future development.​


 ​5​            ​ENVIRONMENTAL AND AESTHETIC IMPACTS (16 TAC § 25.101)​

 ​6​​Q. What are your concerns regarding the local environment and wildlife?​


 ​7​​A. These transmission lines will disturb natural habitat grasses, trees and waterways​

 ​8​​which will move and reduce wildlife in the area.​


 ​9​​Q. How will the line affect the "aesthetic values" (the look and feel) of your area?​


10​​A. These transmission lines will be an eye sore to the property owners who chose to​
​

11​​purchase and maintain rural property, thereby reducing property values.​
​


12​
​                         ​LOCAL NEED AND COST (PURA § 37.056)​

13​​Q. Do you believe this project provides a direct benefit to your local electric​
​

14​​service?​
​


15​​A. No​
​


16​​Q. Do you believe this project will decrease your electric cost?​
​


17​​A. No it is believed this project will increase our costs as the construction fees will be​
​

18​​passed onto the taxpayer/property owners.​
​


19​
​                         ​RECREATION AND COMMUNITY VALUES​


                                                ​Direct Testimony of Hank and Elizabeth Jones, Pro Se​
                                                                              ​PUC Docket No. 59475​
                                                                      ​SOAH Docket No.​​473-26-16349​
                                                                                         ​Page​​8​​of​​11​
  ​1​​Q. How would this transmission line affect your enjoyment of your property?​


 ​2​​A. The proposed transmission line would impact recreational use of firearms, hunting,​

 ​3​​create visual landscape disturbance, reduce farming and ranching use, create​

 ​4​​unnecessary noise and health concerns.​


 ​5​​Q. Do you think the proposed transmission line will affect any planned future use​

 ​6​​on your land?​


 ​7​​A. Yes, the property is listed for sale for development. Easements will reduce the​

 ​8​​number of acres to be available for development.​


 ​9​​Q. How would this transmission line affect your rural community values for your​

10​​area?​
​


11​​A. Transmission line easements reduce acreage use and create visual disturbance in​
​

12​​the country which reduces desire and decreases land sales and community values.​
​


13​
​                        ​CONCLUSIONS AND RECOMMENDATION​

14​​Q. What is your recommendation to the Commission?​
​


15​​A. I recommend the Commission deny the project, seek further state advice on​
​

16​​alternatives or move the project along existing corridors such as state highways.​
​


17​​Q. Does this conclude your testimony?​
​


18​​A.​​Yes.​
​


19​

 ​2​                                        ​PRAYER​

 ​3​​May it please the Commission,​


 ​4​​We thank you for the opportunity to be heard in this matter. We respectfully ask the​

 ​5​​Commission to carefully consider the long-term impacts this proposed transmission line​

 ​6​​may have on our property, our wildlife, our natural waterways, and the rural character of​

 ​7​​our community.​


 ​8​​Our family chose this land as our homestead because of its peace, natural beauty, and​

 ​9​​environmental significance. The proposed route threatens not only the value and​

10​​enjoyment of our property, but also the habitat and historic character that make this area​
​

11​​unique.​
​


12​​We understand the importance of reliable electric infrastructure, but I respectfully submit​
​

13​​that the burden placed on my property and surrounding neighbors and community by​
​

14​​the proposed F8 and F45 routes outweighs any demonstrated local benefit. We ask the​
​

15​​Commission to deny approval of routes utilizing links F8 and F45, or alternatively select​
​

16​​a route that minimizes harm to homes, landowners, wildlife, and environmentally​
​

17​​sensitive areas.​
​


18​​Thank you for your time, consideration and services.​
​


19​
